summary: Off-registry HTTPS tarball dependency with dependency-confusion shape
details: The package ships only an empty stub (index.js exports {}) and a manifest whose sole dependency, `ltidisafe`, is declared as a bare HTTPS tarball URL (https://ltidi.storage.googleapis.com/depenconf/ltidisafe-3.8.9.tgz) rather than a registry version range. On `npm install`, npm fetches whatever bytes that URL serves — unpinned, with no integrity hash, from a bucket outside the npm registry — and runs any lifecycle scripts contained in that tarball on the installer's machine. The scope `@fmr-ap149494`, the implausibly high version `99.9.1`, and the `depenconf` path segment together match the dependency-confusion shape used to win resolution against an internal package name of the same identifier.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
